rationale:
The reviewed tests adequately check `requirements.sdk.outlines.Span`. I judged from the supplied test text only and did not request implementation source.

**Indexing and validity**
- `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[span_indexes_str_at_utf8_byte_boundaries]` uses the multi-byte string "aé🦀".
  - `&source[Span::new(1, 3)]` is "é". This checks byte offsets, an inclusive start and an exclusive end.
  - `&source[Span::new(7, 7)]` is "". This checks an empty span at `len`.
  - It then asserts a panic (via `catch_unwind`) for each of these invalid spans:
    - `Span::new(2, 3)` starts inside "é".
    - `Span::new(0, 2)` ends inside "é".
    - `Span::new(2, 2)` is an empty span inside "é".
    - `Span::new(0, 8)` has `end > len`.
    - `Span::new(3, 1)` has `start > end`.
  - Together these cover each clause of the validity rule: `start <= end`, `end <= len`, and UTF-8 boundaries at both offsets.
  - They also cover the rule that `&source[span]` has the same bounds and boundary checks as `&source[span.start..span.end]`. A lenient implementation, for example one that clamps or returns an empty string, would fail the panic assertions. An inclusive end offset would fail the "é" result.

**Offsets from the original snapshot, including nested items**
- `fn[unicode_spans_use_bytes_and_whitespace_only_lines_create_no_items]` asserts exact byte spans from `OutlineContent`: `Span::new(0, source.len())`, `Span::new(0, 2)` and `Span::new(6, 10)`. The source contains "é" and "🦀", so these are byte offsets rather than character offsets. It also asserts that `&source[item.span]` equals the selected item's text.
- `fn[setext_sections_inside_directives_lists_and_quotes_retain_container_spans]` covers nested items inside directives, quotes and lists. It checks `item.span.start` and `name_span` against offsets found in the original source, which contains non-ASCII text. It also asserts that `selected.text()` equals `&source[item.span]`. This covers "including when a caller selects a nested item".

**Type shape and trait implementations**
- `Span::new` is used throughout.
- Public `start` and `end` fields are read directly in the setext test (`item.span.start`).
- `PartialEq`, `Eq` and `Debug` are exercised by `assert_eq!` on `Span` values and `Option<Span>`.
- `Copy` and `Clone` are exercised by copying `item.span` out of a borrowed item and reusing `span` in the `catch_unwind` closure.
- `Index<Span> for str` is exercised directly.
- `#[non_exhaustive]` and the exact export are covered at the public-surface level by `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/public_api.rs#fn[public_exports_match_the_appendix]`, which is marked as a test of the public-API requirements. An integration test cannot directly assert `non_exhaustive`, because it would be a compile failure, so this is not a gap.

I found no plausible requirement-violating behavior that these tests would accept.

text: `trust_but_verify::outline::Span` locates text by byte offsets from the start
of the original source snapshot, including when a caller selects a nested item.
`start` is inclusive and `end` is exclusive. A valid span satisfies
`start <= end <= source.len()` and both offsets are UTF-8 character boundaries.
For `source: &str`, `&source[span]` yields the same slice as
`&source[span.start..span.end]`, with the same bounds and boundary checks.
pub fn new(start: usize, end: usize) -> Self;
